- When sentiment is high (≥0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 88.0), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment drops.
- If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over 5+ days, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- Model frequently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon; apply 1–2% downward bias for first 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows strong negative sentiment (e.g., 0.00 for 3+ days), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to reflect risk aversion.
- When sentiment shifts from positive to negative, model lags; forecast should adjust 1–2 days ahead of sentiment change.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days show downward trend, model often fails to capture mean reversion; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to counteract underestimation.
